_preregistration.rung: (a) the detector must return a constructed period on synthetic rings; (b) the local re-run must reproduce share_invariance's stored pooled top1
_preregistration.primary: fraction of local replicas that are periodic crystals (p* > 1 at rep >= 0.9)
_preregistration.why: the remote arm's stored rings are exact period-3 and period-4 crystals whose top1 is 1/period by arithmetic; no local results file stores a ring, so whether the same degeneracy is present locally could not be answered from stored data

verdict: RUNG (a), the detector on constructed rings: constant -> p*=1 rep=1.000 (ok); period3 -> p*=3 rep=1.000 (ok); period4 -> p*=4 rep=1.000 (ok); random -> p*=1 rep=0.333 (ok). The detector returns the period it was handed and finds none in noise. RUNG (b), the local re-run against F130's stored pooled top1: worst error 0.0000 across 24 cells (tolerance 0.05). Same quantity as F130. PRIMARY, local crystal fraction (a replica with p* > 1 at rep >= 0.9): mean 0.0052 over 24 cells; 1 cells contain any crystal at all. Frozen (p* = 1) replicas: mean 0.2292. Local crystals EXIST, so the local share is partly a period readout and F130's interpretation needs amending at the constructions where they appear. SECONDARY, the high-share regime is where a crystal would hide, and it is frozen rather than periodic: pythia-31m r2.T0.02 top1=0.988 frozen=0.94 rep1=0.983; pythia-31m r2.T0.2 top1=0.995 frozen=1.00 rep1=0.992; pythia-160m r2.T0.02 top1=0.905 frozen=0.81 rep1=0.864; pythia-160m r2.T0.2 top1=0.970 frozen=0.94 rep1=0.987; pythia-410m r2.T0.02 top1=0.803 frozen=0.88 rep1=0.943; pythia-410m r2.T0.2 top1=0.853 frozen=0.94 rep1=0.952. A high share carried by adjacent-repeat is one token dominating; a high share with rep1 at zero would have been 1/p of a crystal. FULL GRID, from the lattices share_invariance now stores -- 120 cells, 1920 replicas, no re-run: 2 crystal replicas in 1 cells (0.10%). The largest share any crystal reads is 0.5000, so the mechanism still cannot manufacture a high share -- 1/p is bounded by 1/2 for p > 1, and F130's ranking is carried by shares far above that. This supersedes the 24-cell subset F136 reported: the boundary that said 'on this subset' is now the whole of F130's grid, and it cost a file read rather than a run. SCREEN on F134's top-k grid, from stored scalars and no re-run: 15 of 320 cells CANNOT be excluded by arithmetic -- their top1 sits within 0.02 of a unit fraction AND their distinct count is small enough for 16 replicas of a shared short orbit to produce it. The other 305 are excluded outright: pooling over replicas means a 1/period reading needs the SAME dominant token in every replica, which forces a small distinct count, and theirs is far too large. Those 15 were then re-run WITH state: 0 are balanced cycles, 0 are dominated rings whose defects align at some period, 240 are neither. The top-k interface does not reproduce the remote arm's degeneracy. CONTRAST, the remote arm through the same detector: 3 of 6 miss-free cells are periodic crystals -- 8b.r2.T0.2 p*=3 rep=1.00 top1=0.3333 vs 1/p*=0.3333; 8b.r3.T0.2 p*=4 rep=1.00 top1=0.2500 vs 1/p*=0.2500; 8b.r3.T0.2 p*=4 rep=1.00 top1=0.2500 vs 1/p*=0.2500. On those cells top1 IS 1/period by arithmetic and carries nothing about attraction. A further 5 of 11 remote cells lost most of their updates to provider errors and are not settles at all; two of them are byte-identical rings at two different temperatures. AND A THIRD REMOTE DEFECT, independent of the other two: with a 6-word alphabet top1 cannot go below 0.1667, and every remote cell sat in [0.1667, 0.3333] -- the bottom sixth of its range. That is restriction of range on the readout itself, the defect class this project keeps recording, and it was designed in when the alphabet was chosen. BOUNDARY: the local arm is 6 models x 4 constructions at one seed, chosen to span F130's top1 range, not F130's whole grid. It bounds the defect to the remote construction ON THIS SUBSET. The remote arm is 11 cells on two models and is read here only as a contrast -- its own scaffold rung (F135) already failed, so no model claim is drawn from it in any case.
